name: Sengled Zigbee Color A19 (US)

radios.note: Zigbee only; Sengled sells this bulb as 'Hub Required'.

matter.note: Sengled sells it as a Zigbee, hub-required bulb and does not mention Matter. We found no explicit statement or CSA listing either way.

apple_home.note: Sengled does not list Apple Home for this bulb; no official source either way.

google_home.note: Sengled's guide links the Sengled Home account (hub and its bulbs) to Google Home, so it depends on Sengled's cloud. Google Home speakers are not Zigbee hubs.

alexa.note: Sengled lists Echo models with a built-in Zigbee hub (Echo Plus, Echo Show 2, Echo Studio). Echo and Echo Dot are not hubs. The Sengled Alexa skill route was reportedly withdrawn in 2025 (see caveats).

smartthings.note: Sengled lists the SmartThings hub as compatible and documents pairing.

home_assistant.note: No official Home Assistant or Sengled source names this bulb; a generic Zigbee coordinator likely works but is unconfirmed.

hubRequired.note: For bulbs, this means needing a bridge or hub for basic app control. This Zigbee bulb needs a Sengled hub, SmartThings hub or Zigbee Echo.

localControl.note: No official source describes local control. The Sengled app path depends on Sengled's cloud; third-party Zigbee hubs may differ.

lumens.note: 800 lm per Sengled's starter-kit listing for the same Zigbee Color A19/E26 bulb; the single-bulb page gives 8.6 W (60 W equivalent) but no lumen figure.

summary: Nothing controls the Sengled Zigbee Color A19 (E11-N1EAW) without a Zigbee hub. SmartThings works through a SmartThings hub, Alexa through an Echo with a built-in Zigbee hub (Echo Plus, Echo Show 2, Echo Studio), and Google Home through a Sengled Smart Hub linked via Sengled's cloud. Apple Home and Home Assistant are unconfirmed. It's a US full-colour bulb on an E26 base, rated at 800 lumens, with 16 million colours plus tunable white. Amazon reportedly withdrew the Sengled Alexa skill in 2025, so pairing directly to a Zigbee Echo is the Alexa route that doesn't rely on Sengled's account.
caveats: Zigbee only: it needs a Zigbee hub and has no Wi-Fi or Bluetooth.
Amazon removed the Sengled Alexa skill in 2025, according to a PCWorld report citing a series of Sengled service outages.
Google Home control goes through Sengled's cloud, so it depends on that service being up.
A regular Echo or Echo Dot can't control it; you need an Echo model with a built-in Zigbee hub.
